audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart (phases[N].side) disagreed with the content-layer win[N] on all seven rows, and win[N] matches the packet levelChart.
audit.why: Difficulty is real: Gravity Field (800 range, 17/16/15/14/13s) and Hextech Ray (525 range, 12/11/10/9/8s) outrange Ekko's 325-range Phase Dive, so levels 3-5 belong to Viktor; from 6 onward Chronobreak and the W stun cancelling his channelled ult flip it.
audit.corrected: Full-layer sides realigned to Skill/Skill/Viktor/Viktor/Ekko/Ekko/Ekko with ratings and whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and spikes[3] used the fabricated names 'Chaos Storm' and 'Death Ray'.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon gives Viktor R = Arcane Storm (120/100/80s, channel) and E = Hextech Ray.
audit.corrected: Real names used; the 120s ult cooldown and its channel status added to the level 6 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page stated that Arcane Storm is a channel, that Siphon Power shields as it lands, or that Siphon Power is an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: All three are in the kit flags and all three decide when Ekko may commit.
audit.corrected: Parallel Convergence's stun cancels Arcane Storm outright; Siphon Power shields through the opening of your string, so force it out first; his combo opens on an auto reset, so the wind-up is the cue to step back.

audit.why: It is the field that holds real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Gravity Field 17s rank 1, Hextech Ray 12s rank 1, Arcane Storm 120s and channelled.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim (lint: COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2).
audit.why: The title promised one thing and the body explained another.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to match their titles with Phase Dive and Chronobreak cooldowns.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are close, with both champions relying on basic poke and farm patterns without a clear structural edge. By level 3-5, Viktor's augmented kit — especially Gravity Field zoning and Death Ray poke — starts to punish Ekko for standing in the wave or diving carelessly, giving Viktor the edge in a phase where his siege potential outpaces Ekko's early trading tools.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are close, both farming with basic poke while Siphon Power's shield blunts whatever chip Ekko lands. By level 3-5 Viktor's zoning takes over — Gravity Field on a 17s cooldown stuns anyone who lingers in it and Hextech Ray chips every 12s — so Ekko has no safe way to step into 325-range Phase Dive until those are spent, and Viktor owns the wave and the tempo meanwhile.

edits.before: Level 6 tips further toward Viktor: Chaos Storm adds a huge AoE damage-over-time zone that can shred Ekko if he commits an all-in without tracking the cooldown, making this one of the scarier windows in the matchup. Ekko has to play patiently here, using Timewinder to poke from outside Gravity Field range and waiting for Viktor's cooldowns before looking for anything aggressive.
edits.after: Level 6 tips toward Ekko: Arcane Storm is a 120s channel and Parallel Convergence's stun cancels it outright, so Viktor's scariest window becomes Ekko's best one. Bank the W on his retreat line, poke with Timewinder from outside the 800-range Gravity Field, and open the all-in the moment his stun zone is spent rather than trading into a loaded kit, since Siphon Power shields the first hit.

edits.before: Once Ekko lands his first burst item, the matchup flips — his combo (E-slow, Q, W-stun, R) threatens to one-shot Viktor, who has no dash or blink to escape a well-timed dive, so Ekko can punish any overextension hard. Late game, Ekko's mobility and Chronobreak reset let him flank around Viktor's frontal zone control entirely, picking him off in skirmishes before Death Ray or Chaos Storm ever get to punish the engage.
edits.after: Once Ekko lands his first burst item, the matchup flips — his combo (E, Q, W-stun, R) threatens to one-shot Viktor, who has no dash or blink to escape a well-timed dive, so Ekko can punish any overextension hard. Late game, Ekko's mobility and Chronobreak reset let him flank around Viktor's frontal zone control entirely, picking him off in skirmishes before Hextech Ray or Arcane Storm ever get to punish the engage.
